title: Stages of Child Development: Prenatal and Birth to Three Years
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper

extending the arms when support from the neck is removed
babies trying to grasp a finger put in the palm

options: the time the zygote attaches to the uterine wall
the period from conception to 8 weeks
the thick, blood-rich tissue that lines the wall of the uterus

questions.q: What is the primary focus of the embryonic stage of prenatal development?
options: Rapid growth of bones and muscles

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (match the columns, true/false, fill in the blanks or one-word answers).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The placenta is a thick, blood-rich tissue lining the wall of the ________. (ii) As children reach their first birthday, their actions become ________ oriented.
questions.note: Part (i) was asked in April 2025 and part (ii) in October 2024.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) A ________-month-old child can stand holding furniture. (ii) Between two and three years, most toddlers learn about ________ words.
Match: (a) Moro reflex (b) Babinski reflex — (i) Turns the head when the cheek is touched (ii) Extends the arms when support from the neck is removed (iii) Fans out the toes when the foot is stroked
Match: (a) Zygote (b) Implantation — (i) Result of fertilisation (ii) When the zygote attaches to the uterine wall (iii) Eight weeks
State True or False: (i) Toddlers can pick up toys while standing. (ii) Three-year-olds do not recognise themselves in a mirror.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False — toddlers recognise themselves in a mirror.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Babies born before 36 weeks of gestation are considered preterm. (ii) The umbilical stub usually falls off within three weeks of birth.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What period does infancy encompass? Write any two reflexes of infants.
questions.answer: Infancy is the period from birth to one year. Reflexes (any two): rooting, sucking, palmar grasp, Moro, Babinski, startle, eye blink, stepping, swimming.

questions.q: What are some inherited reflexes displayed by infants at birth?
questions.answer: Sucking (sucks at whatever touches the lips), blinking (shuts eyes in bright light) and grasping (closes fingers on an object in the palm); also rooting, Moro, Babinski, startle and stepping.

questions.q: What are infants sensitive to in terms of visual stimuli at birth?
questions.answer: They are sensitive to light-dark visual contrasts and to movement, and show a clear preference for gazing at the human face.

questions.q: What is the sleeping pattern of newborns?
questions.answer: Most newborns wake every two to three hours through day and night; short stretches of sleep alternate with short periods of wakefulness, mainly for feeding and keeping dry and warm. Babies sleep about 18 hours a day.

questions.q: What is the foetal stage?
questions.answer: The last stage of prenatal development, from two months after conception until birth, when sex organs form, bones and muscles grow quickly, the foetus moves and organ systems begin to work.
questions.note: October 2022 asked for a one-sentence explanation.

questions.q: How do drugs influence growth and development at the prenatal stage?
questions.answer: Drugs are teratogens: medical drugs such as some antibiotics and illegal drugs such as marijuana, opiates and cocaine can harm the foetus, causing physical deformity, retarded growth or brain damage. Alcohol and smoking slow growth and may cause mental retardation.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Discuss any three characteristics of the newborn with examples.
questions.answer: Umbilical cord: bluish-white; the stub left after cutting dries and falls off within three weeks, becoming the belly button. Skin: wet and coated with white vernix caseosa (an antibacterial barrier), greyish-blue until breathing starts. Hair: fine body hair called lanugo on the back, shoulders and face, disappearing within weeks. Others: a large head for the body, weight of 2.5–3.5 kg, waking every two to three hours, and inborn reflexes.

or.q: Discuss any three milestones of language development of 2–3-year-old children.
or.answer: Any three: has a word for almost everything; uses two- or three-word phrases to talk about and ask for things; is understood by family and friends; names objects to ask for them; answers routine questions ('What is your name?'); follows two-step directions ('Find your shoes and get your dress'); begins to use plurals, prepositions ('in the jar'), possessives ('mine'), adjectives and '-ed' for the past tense; enjoys simple stories, songs and rhymes.

questions.q: What are the two important functions of the placenta? Mention the stage of prenatal development in which it forms.
questions.answer: Functions: (1) it passes oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood to the embryo or foetus, nourishing it; (2) it removes waste materials from the embryo or foetus. The placenta forms in the germinal stage (the first two weeks after conception).

or.q: Describe any three reflexes in a newborn.
or.answer: Rooting: the infant turns the head towards anything that touches the cheek. Palmar grasp: closes the fingers and grasps an object placed in the palm. Moro: when support for the head and neck is suddenly removed, thrusts the arms out and seems to grasp. (Others: Babinski — toes fan out when the outer sole is stroked; startle; eye blink; sucking; stepping.)

questions.q: Describe the milestones of development of children from birth to three months.
questions.answer: Motor: lifts and turns the head when on the stomach by three months; stretching and kicking become vigorous; grasps a toy for a few moments. Hearing: within weeks responds to sounds by getting quiet or smiling, especially to the mother's voice. Vision: focuses on the mother's face while feeding; notices interesting sights, colours and shapes. Communication: cries to show needs, smiles on purpose, blows bubbles and coos by two months, imitates expressions and reaches for known adults for comfort.

questions.q: Describe any four milestones of cognitive development of children up to three years.
questions.answer: Any four: object permanence — finds hidden objects; deferred imitation — imitates actions seen earlier (brushing hair, talking on a phone); trial-and-error experiments and goal-directed behaviour; names familiar people and objects and looks at the right toy when named; understands and responds to words and simple commands; distinguishes 'you' and 'me'; begins to match similar objects; pretend play with a second person.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the stages of prenatal development and the factors that can harm the developing embryo or foetus.
questions.answer: Germinal stage (0–2 weeks): a sperm and egg join to form a zygote; about 36 hours later it starts dividing; the ball of cells moves to the uterus and implants about seven days after conception; the placenta forms to nourish the embryo and remove waste. Embryonic stage (to about 8 weeks): all major organs form; the embryo is fragile and about an inch long. Foetal stage (two months to birth): sex organs form, bones and muscles grow, the foetus moves, organ systems begin to function; in the last three months the brain grows fast, fat forms under the skin, and breathing and digestion start working. Harmful factors (teratogens): medical and illegal drugs; alcohol, smoking and excess caffeine, which slow growth and may cause mental retardation; and environmental hazards such as chemicals, radiation and extreme heat, which cause mutations and deformities.

questions.q: Trace the milestones of development during toddlerhood (one to three years).
questions.answer: Physical-motor: gross — walks alone and backwards, picks up toys while standing, pushes and pulls, climbs on and off furniture, begins to run; fine — scribbles and paints, may prefer one hand, grasps and throws a ball, pours out contents, feeds self. Socio-emotional: shows fear, joy and by three complex emotions like jealousy and shame; recognises self in a mirror; identifies family; plays alone or beside others, finds sharing hard; asserts independence by saying 'no'; attached to the primary caregiver. Cognitive: object permanence, deferred imitation, trial-and-error, goal-directed behaviour, names objects, understands 'you' and 'me', short attention span. Language: from two or three words at one to about 300 words by three; two- or three-word phrases, follows simple and two-step commands, starts using plurals, possessives and the past tense.
